author: Madeleine Aggeler
description:
Before online influencers existed, the founding father published an annual wellness pamphlet. I followed his 13 virtues he found necessary for a good life

Benjamin Franklin doesn’t get enough credit. Yes, he was a founding father of the United States; he invented the lightning rod and his face is printed on $100 bills. But rarely is he celebrated for his contributions to the most meaningful field of human achievement: wellness influencing.

Centuries before GRWM videos and scientifically dubious podcasts were a dollar-sign-shaped glint in their creators’ eyes, Franklin was doling out life advice. Under the pseudonym Poor Richard, Franklin published an annual pamphlet and minted maxims like “Diligence is the mother of good luck” and “Fish and visitors stink after three days.”
title: Was Benjamin Franklin the original wellness bro? I lived like him for a day to find out

author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
description:
Health ministry records 272 new infections in October, more than eight times the normal monthly rate

Gaza’s health ministry has issued an epidemic alert after a sharp rise in meningitis infections, with more than 270 new cases reported in October.

Dr Nidal Ghoneim, a senior official at the ministry, said the spread of the disease posed a threat to the lives of hundreds of thousands of people, including children.

Continue reading...
title: Gaza issues meningitis epidemic alert after steep rise in cases

author: Katie Cunningham
description:
The Fox director Dario Russo describes his own film as being ‘about a guy who gets tricked by a talking fox into pushing his fiancee in a magic hole’ – but that is only the beginning

  • Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email

When actor Emily Browning first read the synopsis for The Fox, her response was one of confusion. “I was like, what?” she says, scrunching up her face. “A guy talks to a fox and throws his wife in a hole? Huh?”

Explaining this Australian comedy is not an easy task, even for its writer and director, Dario Russo. “It’s a movie about a guy who gets tricked by a talking fox into pushing his fiancee in a magic hole,” he says. “That’s it. That’s what happens.”
title: Olivia Colman as a fox and Sam Neill as a sweary magpie: this is one of the best Australian movies in years

author: Donna Lu
description:
We are offered a seemingly endless array of drinks and foods that now come with added caffeine

  • Read more in the Antiviral series

Feeling tired and need a pick-me-up, but finding your morning cup of coffee isn’t touching the sides? Instead of the predictable choice (a second coffee), you could instead opt for a seemingly endless array of other drinks and foods that now come with added caffeine.

You might energise yourself ahead of your morning gym session with a few caffeinated scoops of a pre-workout supplement. Afterwards, you could refuel with a caffeinated protein shake, or a protein bar with added guarana – whose seeds contain caffeine.

Continue reading...
title: Caffeine has crept into everything. With all the buzz, are we at risk of too much of a caffeine high? | Antiviral

author: Robert Tait, Washinton
description:
Trump’s reaction to sensitive information that contradicts his worldview mirrors his conduct towards war with Iran

Donald Trump’s unwillingness to heed warnings of suspected Chinese penetration of the tech giant Nvidia follows a pattern of the US president ignoring sensitive intelligence that contradicts his world view.

Trump disregarded repeated information that the company’s co-founder, Jensen Huang, was having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy that threatened to undermine Washington’s geo-strategically vital goal of pipping China for global supremacy in the artificial intelligence race.

Continue reading...
title: The Nvidia case is just the latest episode of Trump disregarding intelligence

author: Andrew Cordon
description:
When Wes Craven’s final slasher film came out, correctly predicting clout-chasing influencers and social media’s corruption of our lives, Instagram was just six months old

  • Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email

It has been almost a year since Australia’s social media ban for under-16s and it seems as though nothing has been able to effectively deter the youth from the slippery slope of internet addiction – even when they have expressed the desire to quit. It’s hard to believe that it has only been a decade since TikTok condemned us to the eternal doomscroll and just over 15 years since Instagram launched. Surely no one predicted just how much the online world would be leeching off of u
title: Scream 4 came out 15 years ago – but its mockery of online brainrot is more spot-on than ever

author: Charlotte Jansen
description:
The Photographers’ Gallery, London
Sanlé Sory is known for his black and white images taken during independence in Burkina Faso – but his colour portraits bring humour, insouciance and joy

Despite his wide renown, there have been hardly any major exhibitions of Sanlé Sory’s work. His last UK show was in 2019, concentrating on the black-and-white images the Burkinabé photographer made in the first two decades after opening his own studio, Volta Photo, in Bobo-Dioulasso in 1960 – a period that coincided with the first two decades of independence in Burkina Faso. This new Photographer’s Gallery show shifts the focus to the 1980s and 1990s, when Sory began working in colour.

It’s easy to see why, even with few exhibitions, Sory has made such an impression on audiences. There are the familiar west African studio photography tropes westerners love, where sound, image, fashion and pose collide. The props are popping, the style is irrepressible, the energy i
title: What happened when the man who took a million photographs embraced colour?

author: Claire Wang
description:
Organizers won key civil liberties protections on election day – and women and Black advocates were at the forefront

Progressives made historic gains in the south during the midterm elections – and Virginia was no exception. The state approved three constitutional amendments protecting civil liberties that have eroded in Trump’s second term: enshrining the rights to abortion and same-sex marriage, and restoring voting rights to those with past felony convictions.

These victories were led by women and Black organizers who say they want to capitalize on the momentum and advocate for policies that expand the protections they secured on election day.

Continue reading...
title: Once ‘capital of the Confederacy’, Virginia enshrines rights to voting, abortion and gay marriage

author: Associated Press
description:
Magistrate judge Matthew Sharbaugh, who approved federal raid on congresswoman’s home, raised concern over implications at time

A magistrate judge who authorized a recent search of Ilhan Omar’s home by federal agents ruled that the Minnesota Democratic congresswoman was entitled to assert her right to privacy protections afforded to sitting members of Congress at the outset of the search, according to court documents unsealed on Monday.

The unsealed filings reveal how federal justice department attorneys and US magistrate judge Matthew Sharbaugh resolved their initial disagreement over the thorny constitutional implications of searching a
title: Judge unseals records on Ilhan Omar’s home search amid constitutional debate

author: Arwa Mahdawi
description:
From the first lady’s Amazon documentary to Barron’s energy drink, the family is raking it in during Donald’s second term. And that includes the president

Melania Trump is not a regular mom. She’s “a very cool mom”. We know this because she says so in her very cool new TV docuseries, which no one asked for, but which Amazon made anyway. I should clarify that Melania: The Series is not to be confused with Melania, the 104-minute-long $75m (£57m) movie Amazon released earlier this year. You know, the one an industry insider called “the most expensive documentary ever made that didn’t involve music licensing”. Various people
title: $150 for photos of Melania looking like a waxwork? Will the Trumps ever run out of money-making ideas? | Arwa Mahdawi

author: Michael Hogan
description:
Viewing figures are up and the new judge has spiced up the show with her wit, charm and articulate appreciation of doughy delights. The stale previous seasons are fast becoming a mere memory

When Nigella Lawson helps crown the new champion of The Great British Bake Off on Tuesday night, two other winners will also be celebrating: the show itself and broadcaster Channel 4. The fabled “Nigella effect” has freshened up a franchise that was beginning to taste distinctly stale.

Having replaced Prue Leith as judge for this 17th edition, alongside the ever-present Paul Hollywood, the domestic goddess has made the cake-making contest essential viewing again. Prompting a public outpouring of love, magisterial Lawson has proved the missing ingredient in the show’s resurgence.

Continue reading...
title: ‘The icing on the cake’: how Nigella saved Bake Off

author: Luke Entwistle
description:
Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad

This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says.

Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last-16. “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had
title: Timothy Weah: ‘I don’t want to beg to be back in the national team’

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Prime minister Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement comes days after the ICJ found Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya minority

Malaysia says it will send thousands of migrants and refugees back to Myanmar, despite acknowledging that many asylum seekers in the country had been victims of “atrocities” carried ​out by the junta in Naypyidaw.

The announcement comes just days after the UN’s highest court ruled Myanmar had committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.

Continue reading...
title: Malaysia to send thousands of migrants back to Myanmar as PM acknowledges junta’s ‘atrocities’

author: Presented by Annie Kelly with Kaamil Ahmed, produced by George McDonagh, Harriet Mogie and Rudi Zygadlo
description:
The international court of justice has for the first time ruled that a state has committed genocide. Yasmin Ullah explains what it means for the Rohingya people, while Kaamil Ahmed lays out how the case unfolded

For seven years, Yasmin Ullah had been part of the delegation arguing that Myanmar had committed genocide – one of the gravest human rights crimes – against Rohingya Muslims.

The genocide has directly affected Yasmin and her family. Last week she was in court to hear the international court of justice’s landmark verdict against Myanmar. “I was really kind of pinching myself. It felt like we were all able to breathe again,” she tells Annie Kelly.

Continue reading...
title: Myanmar has been found guilty of genocide. Should Israel be worried? – podcast

author: Dara Kerr
description:
Huang receives hero’s welcome at firm’s Silicon Valley headquarters as return cements role as key AI figure

Jensen Huang made his return to Nvidia’s headquarters with a hero’s welcome on Monday. Hours earlier he’d been reinstated as the CEO of the world’s most valuable chip company, following a whiplash series of events that involved a romantic affair with a suspected Chinese spy, a drastic plummet in the stock market, and an intervention from Donald Trump.

As Huang entered the company’s Silicon Valley office, wearing his signature dark-colored uniform, crowds of employees rushed to greet him clapping, hollering and chanting: “Jensen, Jensen, Jensen!”

Continue reading...
title: Nvidia rejoices at Jensen Huang’s second coming as White House takes victory lap
